project.name: Abercrombie
project.boundarySource: Resolved named-place location with a conservative strict settlement study buffer
project.researchNotes: Sequential place 10 of 14. Strict settlement merit, See, café-led Eat, all named trail providers, picnic, public visitor parking, public toilets, access, transport, dogs and complete local HES/NRHE construction dates were checked before continuing. Balcaskie House is private related context. St Monans and Pittenweem facilities are not transferred.

touristAppeal.label: Minor Interest
touristAppeal.summary: Abercrombie is a worthwhile specialist heritage stop for its roofless late-medieval church, carved stones and walking connection, but it has no café or public-facility depth and remains selector-only at 56.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: No destination-scale dog visit or dedicated dog facilities are assumed without current evidence.

visitorHighlights.name: Abercrombie Church and Carved Stones
visitorHighlights.reason: A compact and atmospheric medieval church ruin with carved-stone interest, best suited to a specialist short stop.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Outdoor monument and churchyard; visit in daylight and respect any local access notices.
visitorHighlights.sourceName: Fife Walking and Historic Environment Scotland
